title: Results of a generated 8 Direction character
author: Cosmonan
selftext:
After messing around with Pixel Lab Plugin in Aseprite, I was able to make a full 8 Direction character with Attack, Idle, and Movement animations. It can be refined further, and will be, but I liked it a lot for 1-day work. Also got the chance to generate some enemy sprites, and I must say the style tool is pretty good for consistency. 

It's far from a first shot, and needs some good cleaning up in Aseprite, but this is also good for learning while doing I guess.

comments.author: MaleficentClub7480
comments.body: Looks good! What is the „Style Tool“?

replies.author: Cosmonan
replies.body: It's from Pixel Lab plugin in Aseprite. Basically you use around 5-10 reference sprites to create like 30 more (depends on sprite size) based on a text prompt, and the style is maintained.

comments.author: Economy_Pen_458
comments.body:
The graphics look great and the character moves very fluidly; what tool did you use, or how did you create the attack and walking animations?

I’ve tried a few times, but the character always looks stiff or like they’re walking on the same leg.

replies.author: Cosmonan
replies.body:
Thank you! The workflow is basically:

\- generate concept image in ChatGPT (took some tries to realize full symmetrical is a must have prompt for good results)  
\- feed concept image to Pixel Lab (web) character creator: generates 8 directional idle character  
\- create 3 different poses in Pixel Lab (web): Middle Run, Fighting Stance and Middle Punch  
\- generate the animations for run and idle in Pixel Lab (web), until I get at least 3 out of 5 animations (Im mirroring NE, SE and E) good enough.  
\- Import the sprite sheets to Aseprite  
\- clean up Idle and Run animations  
\- In Aseprite Pixel Lab Plugin, I use the Interpolate tool between Fighting Stance and Middle Punch poses to create each direction until I also get some good results. Clean up after.  
\- Mirror 3 lateral directions (E, NE, SE)  
\- This gives me 3 animations in 8 directions

Walking animation just got better after the "Fully Symmetrical" character.

replies.author: Economy_Pen_458
replies.body:
What size sprite are you using?

I actually subscribed to PixelLab's "Apprentice" plan, and the character created is really good, but I couldn't quite manage to create a smooth animation flow :(

replies.author: Cosmonan
replies.body:
64x64 is the way to go. Lower than that and the model will have trouble figuring what is a leg, an arm, etc.

Try making intermediary poses and use interpolation to create the animation. Takes some more time but can give some good results.

replies.author: Economy_Pen_458
replies.body: My plan is still active, so I'll give it a few more tries using the tips you shared—thanks!

comments.author: thetinytrex
comments.body: Been using pixellab too and it works well but oh boy do you need to clean it up. I went through the trouble of making all the animations for my main character but decided to scrap it all so I can do it pixel perfect since I was lazy the first time.

replies.author: Cosmonan
replies.body:
It surely needs a good touch in, I would say, 20% of animations just to look somewhat reasonable.  
For pixel perfect, yeah, 100% I need to remake all of them. I'm at the lazy stage atm hahaha, so I guess I'll be improving over time, I don't plan on having more than 3 or 4 animations per character.  


Also, decided for going with full symmetrical character, so I need to make 5 out of 8 directions only. The first character is also a melee unarmed fighter, so this also helps a little.

comments.author: liatris4405
comments.body: That looks great. The game I’m working on right now is in 3D, but making a pixel art game with AI is incredibly difficult. I honestly never expected 3D to be the easier option.

replies.author: Cosmonan
replies.body:
Ooh, I tried going for 3D before this game, but my troubled mind decided to try a Character Action game from the start lol. I did get some good results, but refining the animation cancel mechanica was soooo intense and demanding, I ended up dropping the idea and going for HD 2D graphics. 

At first I was using only 2 sided sprites, which is honestly not bad for a grid tile game, but I saw some Pixel Lab videos and decided to give a chance to 8 direction.

comments.author: BeltwayBro
comments.body:
This looks awesome!   
  
I've been working on a game and ideally want to get that same consistent 45% isometric look but I am struggling with consistency. Any tips on how you were able to lock that in so nicely?  
  
Also, is there a link where I can play this?

replies.author: Cosmonan
replies.body:
What do you mean by consistent? Consistency between sprites, UI or world?

For UI and world, feeding concept arts (and generating new ones based on current state) usually helps.

For the sprites (character, items and monsters), I'm using Pixel Lab Style tool. I start by making \~15 sprites from text (single prompt so they keep consistency) and then I use the Create from Style tool, by feeding the best sprites from the first batch. You can keep going indefinitely. There are some videos on youtube explaining the concept.

You can try it at [https://tbgallinucci.itch.io/babelum](https://tbgallinucci.itch.io/babelum)

replies.author: BeltwayBro
replies.body:
My main character sprites and animations are fairly consistent -- but my environmental sprite and base map, and enemy sprites -- not so much. 

And cool, thanks for sharing . I willd definetely check this out.
